title: Unary prefix phase
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, let $K$ be a predicate on natural numbers, and let $\sigma=(p,n,a,b,s,t,tmp,st,nx)$ be a nine-register state. Suppose $2|x|+2\le B$, every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $p=2n$, and $p\le |x|$. Assume that for every $n'\ge n$, if $\operatorname{UnaryRest}(x,n,n')$ holds, then the program started at label $m0$ with $p=2n'+2$ and vertex count $n'$ has property $K(n')$. Then the program started at label $u0$ in state $\sigma$ terminates on every branch with all registers at most $B$, and has an accepting branch exactly when there is some $n'\ge n$ for which $\operatorname{UnaryRest}(x,n,n')$ and $K(n')$ both hold.
hypotheses_covered: $K$ is a predicate on natural numbers
Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
For every $n'\ge n$, if $\operatorname{UnaryRest}(x,n,n')$, the indicated $m0$ computation has property $K(n')$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number with $2|x|+2\le B$, let $K$
be a predicate on natural numbers, and let $\sigma$ be a nine-register configuration
whose register values are all at most $B$. Suppose $\sigma.p=2\sigma.n$ and $\sigma.p\le
|x|$. Assume that for every $n'\ge\sigma.n$, if from positions $2i$ and $2i+1$ the
string $x$ has bits $1,1$ for every $\sigma.n\le i<n'$, and has bits $0,1$ at positions
$2n',2n'+1$, then the program started at label $m0$ with input pointer $2n'+2$ and
vertex count $n'$ has property $K(n')$. Then the program started at label $u0$ with
configuration $\sigma$ terminates on every branch with all register values bounded by
$B$, and has an accepting branch exactly when such an $n'\ge\sigma.n$ exists for which
the stated bit conditions and $K(n')$ hold.
